translation_direction: bn → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Bengali electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Amal’s child wonder and relentless questions, Madhav’s anxious tenderness and the villagers’ voices are kept in plain spoken Vietnamese, with the restrained final pages left unexplained.
decisions.rationale: The play’s sorrow depends on what is not said.

decisions.decision: The Bengali text comes from Wikisource because the backlog entry carried no text; it is translated directly from the Bengali.
decisions.rationale: Translation from the original, not from an English version.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘পণ্ডিত’ (the scholars Amal refuses to become) was rendered differently in Acts I and II, losing the echo of the motif; unified as ‘học giả’.
The hour-count rendered as ‘bốn canh’ placed the scene after midnight, contradicting the king’s coming at midnight; now a loose evening time.
The speaker labelled ‘কবিরাজ’ in the source (units 393, 395, 397) is the royal physician; relabelled ‘Ngự y’ and recorded in the glossary.
The palm-leaf umbrella had been rendered as a hat; now a ‘dù lá gồi’.
A calque in the vocative order (‘Amal con’); now ‘Amal con ơi’.
A softening particle added to the closing line; removed to keep the restraint.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: One pair per interlocutor across the three acts.
The scholars who never leave their houses, echoed by Amal.

glossary.draft_rendering: Amal; Madhav; Thakurda; Thầy lang; Ngự y; Trưởng làng; Sudha …
glossary.rationale: Labels kept stable; the royal physician is ‘Ngự y’.

witness_decision: Selected the Bengali Wikisource transcription of ডাকঘর by Rabindranath Tagore (first published 1912), taken from the rendered pages of the three acts; the transcription was not collated with a printed edition by the project.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The logic of unit 321 reads slightly stiff.
A detail (‘đạp tung’) is added in unit 382.
‘Con định gì, con?’ in unit 400 is stilted.

title_review.rationale: The title is translated as ‘Bưu điện’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: Madhav’s worry about the child he has taken in.
The last unit: Sudha’s message to Amal: that Sudha has not forgotten him.
